newsitem.title: NORWAY: NATO ministers, to meet Rodionov, discuss Russia.
newsitem.headline: NATO ministers, to meet Rodionov, discuss Russia.

text.p: NATO defence ministers discussed closer military cooperation with Moscow on Wednesday, the day before a first meeting with Russian Defence Minister Igor Rodionov, NATO officials said.
Rodionov, appointed this summer, will hold talks with the 16 NATO ministers at the end of a two-day informal meeting of the alliance in the Norwegian west coast city of Bergen.
"We have discussed today NATO-Russia relations from a defence point of view," NATO Secretary-General Javier Solana told reporters.
"Tomorrow we will have a meeting with the minister of defence, a newcomer for us. Nobody has had the opportunity of meeting him personally of the 16 ministers of defence," he said.
Russian has expressed serious misgivings about NATO plans to take on some former Soviet bloc states as new members.
"The dialogue between NATO and Russia will be very intense. We will have an open dialogue, a frank dialogue," Solana said.
NATO and Russia have developed a template for military cooperation in peacekeeping operations in Bosnia under the multinational IFOR framework, he said.

"It will also be necessary or may be necessary to underline to Russia that the decision for allowing NATO to grow in size has been taken. There is firm consensus on that subject," British Defence Secretary Michael Portillo said.
"In an uncertain world it is our duty to inject as much certainty and stability as we can. And the certainty we inject is that we will proceed with the timetable for the enlargement of NATO.
German Defence Minister Volker Ruehe said he would take up the issue of Russian membership in a follow-on unit to IFOR once the mandate of the 52,000-member force runs out in December.

A senior U.S. defence official earlier this week said Defence Secretary William Perry looked forward to private talks with Rodionov on continued bilateral and other cooperation, which grew out of close ties between Perry and former Russian Defence Minister Pavel Grachev.
Grachev was sacked by President Boris Yeltsin, who now faces a heart operation, in a domestic shakeup.
Perry has said he understands Russia's concerns about NATO expansion and that he strongly supports proposals for a new NATO charter giving Moscow a non-voting voice in alliance affairs.
